hot_loop_hypothesis.current_verified: Four A object-pointer loads plus four float loads and two unpcklps/one movlhps per k; no hot allocation/call/spill already.
hot_loop_hypothesis.proposed: One F4 pointer load plus unaligned 16-byte vector load from payload offset8, one F10 pointer; ten existing B broadcast/mulps/addps updates unchanged.
hot_loop_hypothesis.tests: Actual object must show packed load, no newly introduced per-k call/alloc/rsp traffic; SIMD instruction count alone cannot prove speedup.

implementation_preconditions: Dispatch to F4 route before global A.map; preserve other routes exactly.
Direct four Float32 scalar fields, not generic Float32 list/tuple/read closure that can introduce transient boxes.
Prepare from original raw A with identical ExecFloat.Binary.toFloat32 decoder, outside the g-column loop.
Borrow panel across all G column groups; release after finishing output for this four-row block; do not first materialize a global Vector of all panels.
Keep global packedB and original raw inputs for the exact existing output NaN replay.
No tail padding/reordering accepted without proof; no-tail initial guard m%4==0 can reduce obligations but greatly reduces coverage.
Retain huge Nat/USize bounds and old fallback, original per-lane k order, +0 seeds, signed-zero normalization and original NaN result policy.
proof_obligations: For b,q,r<4,k<n: packA.get k field r equals ExecFloat.Binary.toFloat32 A[((b*m+4*q+r)*n)+k].
Pointwise F4 four-row loop equals existing scalar/native loop for each row/column with the same k accumulation sequence; storage regrouping alone does not prove native NaN/payload equivalence.
Reuse existing F10 lane correspondence, final native nonNaN bridge and original raw replay independently for each output.
Prove row-major output emission and complete-row/tail partition; m%4!=0 tail and giant dimension cases retain prior exact path.
